requirement_text.REQ-070: Replace lib/letflow/router.ex's single flat route table -- today GET /health plus a 404 catch-all, per its own moduledoc -- with the decomposed structure the rest of S4 mounts into. This resolves stage-4-api-surface.md's OQ-1. The shape is per-subsystem sub-routers under an /api/v1 prefix, one module per R-Co route file group, delegated to from a top-level router. Framework: Plug/Bandit (REQ-065 addendum 2026-08-20). GET /health preserved byte-compatibly (200+{"status":"ok"}, no auth, no DB). Unmatched routes return REQ-066 RFC 9457 404. Shared middleware chain declared in exactly one place.

task.description:
WF-02 Step 2c — HARD GATE: Security review for REQ-070 (router decomposition).

Read docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md before reviewing.
Read all 12 changed/created files directly — do not rely on ELIXIR-DEV's summary.

This requirement is router wiring only — no new business logic, no Ecto queries, no auth decisions, no tenant data handling. Check the following invariants against the actual code:

INV-1 (Tenant isolation): Does the tenant-scoped middleware pipeline (Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline) mount AuthPipeline and TenantStatus BEFORE any sub-router forward? Is there any path to a tenant-scoped sub-router that bypasses this pipeline?

INV-2 (Row-level authorization): Not applicable here — no Ecto queries introduced.

INV-3 (Input validation): Does Plug.Parsers have a length cap configured? What is the cap? Is it a named constant or a buried literal?

INV-4 (No secret leakage in errors): Does the catch-all 404 path go through Letflow.Api.Response.not_found/1 (REQ-066 contract)? Does the health endpoint emit exactly {"status":"ok"} with no stack traces, DB state, or internal info?

INV-5 (No 403 leaking existence to cross-tenant callers): Not applicable for this requirement's own code — it is wiring, not a resource handler. But check: does anything in the router structure make it possible to distinguish a not-found from a forbidden resource at the routing layer? (It should not — all unrouted paths get a uniform 404.)

INV-6 (Auth token handling): Does Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline remain the only place that reads/validates auth tokens? Is there any new token-inspection code in router.ex, api_pipeline.ex, or any sub-router stub?

INV-7 (No SQL interpolation): Not applicable — no SQL in any changed file.

INV-8 (No unhandled crash on malformed input): Does the JSON parser have a :length cap so an oversized request body is rejected with 413 rather than being buffered? Is Plug.Parsers configured to handle malformed JSON gracefully (it is — Plug.Parsers catches parser errors and returns 400 by default)?

Additional checks:
- Is GET /health genuinely outside the tenant-scoped middleware chain? Verify by tracing the request path: Letflow.Router receives /health, matches it directly, returns the response — it NEVER reaches Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline. A request to /api/v1/* DOES reach ApiPipeline and its AuthPipeline/TenantStatus chain.
- Are there any hardcoded credentials, tokens, or secrets in any of the 12 files?
- Does any sub-router stub expose a path that could be reached without going through the shared middleware?

FAIL immediately on any invariant violation. No partial credit.

Complete the handoff: status COMPLETED, result.status PASS or FAIL. On FAIL: list violations by INV number in result.issues at BLOCKER severity, next_action 'Rework ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a rework)'. On PASS: next_action 'Route to REVIEWER (Step 2d)'. Commit the completed handoff on branch feature/WF02-REQ070-20260821 by explicit path.
acceptance_criteria: INV-1: AuthPipeline and TenantStatus are mounted before any sub-router forward in ApiPipeline
INV-3: Plug.Parsers has a length cap configured
INV-4: No internal state or stack traces in 404 or health responses
INV-6: No new token-inspection code outside AuthPipeline
INV-8: Length cap prevents large body buffering
GET /health is outside the tenant-scoped middleware chain
No hardcoded credentials in any changed file

result.summary: All applicable invariants PASS. This change is router wiring only — no Ecto queries, no migrations, no secret resolution, no new token-inspection code. Scope test: change touches the middleware pipeline that gates all tenant-scoped routes, so INV-1, INV-3, INV-4, INV-5, INV-6, and INV-8 apply and were checked against the actual diff. INV-2 (row-level authorisation) and INV-7 (SQL interpolation) are NOT-APPLICABLE (no Ecto queries or SQL in any changed file).

invariant_assessments.evidence: lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex plug order: Plug.Parsers → Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline → Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus → :match → :dispatch → forward/2 calls. AuthPipeline and TenantStatus execute before any sub-router forward by construction. GET /health is handled in Letflow.Router before the forward("/api/v1", ...) line, so it never reaches ApiPipeline — confirmed by route ordering in router.ex. All 10 sub-router stubs declare only plug(:match) + plug(:dispatch); they carry no plug chains of their own and cannot bypass the ApiPipeline middleware already applied.
No Ecto queries, schema modules, or response-shaping code in any of the 12 changed files.

api_pipeline.ex line: plug(Plug.Parsers, parsers: [:json], json_decoder: Jason, length: 2_097_152). Cap is 2,097,152 bytes (2 MB). Inline integer literal with a comment: '2 MB cap — matches R-Co's max_body_size default'. Not a named module constant (@attribute), but the value is documented and justified in the comment.

Health endpoint emits exactly Letflow.Api.Response.send_json(conn, 200, %{status: "ok"}) — no DB, no config, no internal state, no stack traces. All catch-all 404 paths (both in Letflow.Router and Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline and all 10 stubs) call Letflow.Api.Response.not_found(conn) which takes only the conn — no detail argument, so no exception message, Ecto error, or stacktrace can reach the response body (confirmed by reading response.ex: not_found/1 calls Error.not_found() with no args). Secret grep (grep -rniE '(password|secret|client_secret|token)\s*(=|:)\s*"[^"]{8,}' across all 12 files) returned no matches.

No HTTP 403 is emitted at the routing layer. All unrouted paths go through Letflow.Api.Response.not_found/1 (uniform 404). A caller cannot distinguish an unrecognised path from a forbidden path at this layer. Full INV-5 (cross-tenant lookup-by-ID indistinguishability) remains deferred until S4 lookup handlers are added.

invariant_assessments.verdict: APPLIES (meta-invariant: proof of scoping for new data-access path setup) — PASS
invariant_assessments.evidence: No new token-inspection or credential-reading code in any of the 12 files. Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline remains the sole auth handler. The sub-router stubs introduce no data-access paths — they are empty catch-all stubs. This SECURITY-REVIEWER handoff constitutes the required proof record for the new routing structure.
No SQL in any changed file.

Plug.Parsers length: 2_097_152 cap means a request body exceeding 2 MB raises Plug.Parsers.RequestTooLargeError, which implements the Plug.Exception protocol (status 413) and is caught by Bandit before any application code processes the body — large bodies are never buffered. Malformed JSON raises Plug.Parsers.ParseError (implements Plug.Exception, status 400) — default behaviour preserved; no custom error handler or :pass option is specified in api_pipeline.ex that would override this. Neither error propagates as an unhandled crash.

additional_checks.health_outside_middleware: PASS — GET /health matched in Letflow.Router before forward("/api/v1", ...), never reaches ApiPipeline.
additional_checks.no_hardcoded_secrets: PASS — secret grep returned no matches across all 12 files.
additional_checks.stubs_no_bypass: PASS — all 10 stubs contain only plug(:match) + plug(:dispatch) + catch-all 404; no plug chains of their own.
